Notes to Consolidated Unaudited Statement of Financial Results for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026

1. The statement of consolidated unaudited financial results for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026, have been reviewed by Audit Committee and approved by Board of Directors at its meeting held on November 13, 2026. The Statutory Auditors of the Company have carried out limited review on the above results in terms of Regulation 33 of the SEBI (Listing Obligation and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 ('the Regulation'), as amended and expressed an unmodified conclusion.

2. The statement of consolidated unaudited financial results of the Company have been prepared in accordance with the recognition and measurement principles laid down in the Indian Accounting Standard 34 'Interim Financial Reporting', prescribed under Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013 read with relevant rules issued thereunder and other recognised accounting principles generally accepted in India and in terms of the Regulation.

3. During the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026, the Company has allotted 22,83,333 and 27,83,333 fully paid-up equity shares of face value Re. 1 each (“Equity Shares”) respectively, at a securities premium of Rs. 51 per Equity Share, pursuant to the exercise of stock options by employees in accordance with the Company's stock option scheme.

4. On April 7, 2015, the Company acquired the Film and Media Services business from Reliance MediaWorks Limited (RMW) under a BTA dated November 19, 2014, for equity consideration of Rs. 35,000 lakhs, with a conditional obligation to assume debt facilities of Rs. 20,000 lakhs. Subsequently, the Company entered into a Loan Agreement dated February 25, 2019, with Raspalfa Services Private Limited (RASPL), for Rs. 20,000 lakhs.

Conclusion of IBC Proceedings:

On August 29, 2023, RASPL filed a Section 7 petition under the IBC before the NCLT for Rs. 35,379.75 lakhs alleging default under the Loan Agreement.

The NCLT admitted the petition and initiated CIRP on May 6, 2026. On May 12, 2026, the NCLAT stayed the order and directed a deposit of Rs. 35,379.75 lakhs, placed in a fixed deposit with the Registrar, NCLAT.

On July 10, 2026, the NCLAT set aside the NCLT order, approved the Discharge Agreement dated July 1, 2026, for Rs. 40,800 lakhs towards full and final settlement, closed the CIRP and released the fixed deposit.

The fixed deposit of Rs. 35,379.75 lakhs was released and the balance Rs. 5,420.25 lakhs was paid during the quarter ended September 30, 2026, thereby completing the settlement of Rs. 40,800 lakhs.

As at March 31, 2026, the Company had accrued Rs. 35,379.75 lakhs. The additional impact of Rs. 7,335.63 lakhs (including legal and professional fees and tax-related expenses) was recognised as an exceptional item during the half year ended September 30, 2026, comprising Rs. 7,144.05 lakhs in the quarter ended June 30, 2026, and Rs. 191.58 lakhs in the quarter ended September 30, 2026.


5. PF Media Ltd, an indirect subsidiary of the Company has been voluntarily liquidated with effect from July 13, 2026, and accordingly a resultant net gain on liquidation of Rs. 595.88 Lakhs is included in exceptional item in the statement of consolidated unaudited financial results for the half year ended September 30, 2026.

6. Subsequent to the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026, the Income Tax Department, Mumbai ("the Department"), conducted search and seizure activity (“the search”) under the provisions of the Income Tax Act, 2025, at certain offices of the Holding Company and its subsidiaries, as well as at the residences of certain directors of the Holding Company from October 7, 2026, to October 14, 2026. The Department also seized certain electronic records (including information in electronic form and on computer systems) during the search.

The Group has provided all necessary cooperation, documents and details to the Department, as requested and the Holding Company has intimated stock exchanges on October 14, 2026. As at the date of these financial results, the Group has not received any order, demand, show-cause notice or other communication in relation to the Search. The Holding Company, after considering all available information and facts as of date, has not identified the need for any adjustments to the current or prior period financial results. The Holding Company will continue to monitor the developments and will take appropriate actions.

7. Exchange (loss) / gain (net) includes unrealised exchange gain/(loss) arising from the translation of foreign currency denominated borrowings at the closing exchange rates prevailing at the respective reporting dates.

8. Operating segments are reported in a manner consistent with internal reporting provided to the Chief Operating Decision Maker (“CODM”) (i.e., the Board of Directors) of the Group. The CODM is responsible for allocating resources and assessing performances of the operating segments of the Group. The Group is mainly engaged in operating as integrated post-production setup. The CODM decides on allocation of the resources to the business taking a holistic view of the entire setup and hence it is considered as representing a single operating segment as per IND AS 108 “Segment Reporting”.

9. On June 26, 2026, Double Negative Films Limited ("DNFL"), an indirect subsidiary of the Company, acquired a 48.45% equity stake in Anima Kitchent Canarias, S.L. ("Anima"), an entity incorporated in Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, Spain, in partnership with Sociedad Española para la Transformacion Tecnologica (a Spanish Government Fund, "SETT"), for an initial investment of Euro 1.275 million (approximately Rs.13.69 crore), thereby obtaining joint control over Anima. The investment has been classified as a joint venture and accounted for using the equity method. The unaudited consolidated financial results include the Group's share of loss from the joint venture for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026 from the date of acquisition of the joint control.

10. Brahma AI Holdings Limited (“BHL”), and Brahma AI Services India Limited (Formerly known as Prime Focus Technologies Limited) (“Brahma India”), both are subsidiaries of DNEG S.a.r.l, and indirect subsidiaries of the Company have proposed to raise an aggregate investment of USD 100 million from Multiples Private Equity Gift Fund IV (Investment of USD 54.36 million in BHL) and Multiples Private Equity Fund IV (Investment of USD 45.64 million in Brahma India) (collectively referred to as “Multiples”) through the issuance of Compulsorily Convertible Preference Shares (“CCPS”).

The proposed transaction also envisages the transfer of DNEG S.a.r.l's shareholding in Brahma India to BHL. Upon completion of the transaction and implementation of the related governance arrangements, BHL and Brahma India are expected to cease being subsidiaries and become associates of the Group.

On November 7, 2026, the shareholders of the Company approved the proposed cessation of exercise of control over BHL and, consequently, Brahma India, being unlisted material subsidiaries of the Company. However, the transaction remains subject to the fulfilment of certain other conditions precedent specified in the respective agreements and has not been completed as at the date of approval of these unaudited consolidated financial results.

11. Figures for the previous periods have been regrouped/reclassified to conform to the classification of the current periods, if any.

12. The above consolidated unaudited statement of financial results of the Group is available on the Company's and stock exchanges websites (www.primefocus.com), BSE (www.bseindia.com) and NSE (www.nseindia.com), where the shares of the Company are listed.
